title: Blink Timing Explorer
description: Simulates the Pico 2 blink loop as a scrolling voltage-versus-time square wave so students can connect the sleep() argument to an observable blink rate.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Microcontrollers

educational.topic: Digital output timing and blink frequency
learningObjectives: Calculate blink frequency from a given sleep() delay argument
Explain why one blink cycle requires two pin toggles
Predict the square-wave shape produced by a chosen delay
prerequisites: Digital output pins have two voltage states

controls.label: Run / Pause
controls.purpose: Start or stop the automatic toggle-and-delay loop

controls.label: Toggle Once
controls.purpose: Pause and perform exactly one pin state flip

controls.label: Show code
controls.purpose: Reveal the simulated loop with the live delay value

assumptions: Loop and toggle overhead are negligible compared to the sleep interval
limitations: Does not model interpreter overhead, which makes real MicroPython blink rates slightly slower than the ideal formula

keyQuestions: Why does one blink require two toggles?
What delay produces exactly 5 blinks per second?
commonMisconceptions: That sleep(0.5) yields 2 blinks per second rather than 1
assessmentOpportunities: Predict blinks per second before moving the slider
